item.title: NT Government’s rushed remote rental amendments criticised by Aboriginal groups
item.description: The CLP Government's rushed amendments to the Housing Act that will continue to see individual remote housing residents not consulted on rent increases has been panned by Aboriginal land councils and other bodies as an "assault on the fundamental rights of Territorians", while the government claims it will consult with the groups before future rental rises.

item.title: Connolly appointment costing Lia and CLP politically while sowing deep division across the Territory
item.description: EDITORIAL: Chief Minister Lia Finocchiaro’s defence of choosing David Connolly as Administrator this week has done nothing to calm rising tensions in the wider community and instead raised questions about what type of agenda she's driving that was not fully disclosed to Territorians ahead of the last NT election.

item.title: Man arrested for alleged indecent assault at campground
item.description: A 55-year-old man has been charged with gross indecency without consent in relation to an alleged indecent assault at a roadhouse campground in the Barkly region on Friday night, NT Police said.

item.title: Singleton Station water licence decision taken to High Court
item.description: The NT Government's decision to approve a 30-year water licence to Fortune Agribusiness for its Singleton Station project will now be considered by the High Court, following a challenge by native title holders from the Mpwerempwer Aboriginal Corporation.

item.title: NT Criminal Court list – with charges – Feb 11
item.description: The 280 names facing criminal courts in the Northern Territory for Wednesday, February 11, 2026. This list includes all the charges.

item.title: Greens Member for Nightcliff resigns
item.description: UPDATED: Kat McNamara, the first NT Greens member elected to NT Parliament, has resigned "effective immediately", citing health reasons, while a federal senator says McNamara was insulted and "intimidated" by government while in Parliament.

item.title: Alice Springs woman sexually assaulted while putting child into vehicle
item.description: A woman securing her child into her vehicle at a Gregory Terrace carpark in Alice Springs just after noon on Monday was allegedly indecently assaulted by a male youth, with police now calling for the public's help to identify the male.

item.title: Half of Health’s Acacia IT system shelved pending new funding despite risk of ‘catastrophic failure’ of systems
item.description: Half of the controversial $320 million NT Health Acacia patient record IT system is being shelved pending new funding approvals, bureaucrats have told a parliamentary committee, despite their own previous warnings that not fully implementing it risks a "catastrophic IT systems failure" that could disrupt health services.

item.title: ‘Detrimental change’: NT Police’s Darwin property and juvenile crime unit to be moved
item.description: Darwin's property and juvenile crime police unit, Strike Force Trident, is being moved from the Casuarina Police Station to be absorbed by the Crime and Intelligence Command at the Peter McCauley Centre, the police union has said, a move the man who established the unit said could see members siphoned off to other parts of the agency due to political pressures, leading to a potential increase in property crime.

item.title: ICAC releases investigation findings into NT WorkSafe conflicts of interest, failure to manage staff
item.description: The Independent Commissioner Against Corruption has disclosed the findings of its investigation into allegations NT WorkSafe's electrical inspectors unit misused statutory powers, failed to manage conflicts of interest and failed to disclose secondary employment with commercial electrical companies the workplace regulator may have investigated.
